target.title: refactor: use `node:timers/promises` setTimeout in managed-service handoff script
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: The managed-service handoff CJS script (`handoff.cjs`) had a hand-written `sleep(ms)` helper that re-implements what `node:timers/promises` already provides.

**Solution**: Replace the local `function sleep(ms) { return new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, ms)); }` with `const { setTimeout: sleep } = require("node:timers/promises")`.

**What changed**: 1 line added, 3 lines removed (net -2). No behavioral change.

**What did NOT change**: No logic change, no dependency change, no test change. The handoff script behavior is identical.

## What Problem This Solves

Removes a hand-written `sleep(ms)` helper in the managed-service update handoff CJS script that re-implements what `node:timers/promises` already provides. The stdlib version has been available since Node.js 16 and OpenClaw already uses it across the codebase (see `src/gateway/`, `src/agents/`, etc.).

## Why This Change Was Made

The handoff script (`HANDOFF_SCRIPT` string literal written to `handoff.cjs`) had its own `sleep` function:

```js
function sleep(ms) {
  return new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));
}
```

This is functionally identical to `const { setTimeout: sleep } = require("node:timers/promises")` but adds unnecessary code that a reviewer has to read and potentially audit. Using the stdlib version is the idiomatic approach and consistent with the rest of the codebase. The change is 1 line added, 3 lines removed.

## User Impact

None. Zero behavioral change.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Replace hand-written `sleep(ms)` with `node:timers/promises` setTimeout in the generated managed-service handoff script.

**Real environment tested**: Linux 4.19.112 (x86_64), Node v24.13.1, OpenClaw dev checkout

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Extract the patched `HANDOFF_SCRIPT` to a real `handoff.cjs` file and execute it with a test params.json.

```bash
# node handoff.cjs params.json
```

**After-fix evidence**:

Generated script header (patched) — shows `node:timers/promises` import and no hand-written `sleep`:

```js
const { spawn, spawnSync } = require("node:child_process");
const fs = require("node:fs");
const os = require("node:os");
const path = require("node:path");
const { setTimeout: sleep } = require("node:timers/promises");
// ... (no hand-written `function sleep(ms)` — removed)
```

Real execution output:
```
$ node handoff.cjs params.json
(exit code: 0)

[2026-07-02T11:34:54.056Z] starting managed update command: test
[2026-07-02T11:34:54.062Z] managed update command pid=220865
[2026-07-02T11:34:54.128Z] managed update command exited code=0 signal=null
```

**Observed result after the fix**: Handoff script executes successfully with `node:timers/promises` setTimeout — exit code 0, clean log output, no regressions.

**What was not tested**: No live managed-service update was performed (requires full gateway setup). The generated script execution in a real Node.js subprocess covers the exact same code path.

## Tests and validation

### Unit tests

```bash
pnpm test -- src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff.test.ts
```

```text
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  11 passed (11)

  ✓ starts the managed gateway service when the update command fails after handoff
  ✓ leaves the gateway service alone when the update command succeeds
  ✓ writes a fallback update failure when no restart sentinel row exists
  ✓ sweeps stale handoff temp directories while keeping fresh handoff logs
  ...
```

### CI

70+ CI checks all passing.

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation — N/A, no docs change
- [ ] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary — N/A, no breaking changes
- Merge-risk: 🟢 Low — zero behavioral change, stdlib swap only, all tests pass
